gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, in named tests, the Apex 300's UPS transfer measured 16 ms rather than the 0 ms BLUETTI advertises (StorageReview). Nor does any state that the Apex 200 idles at 12.8 W against about 20 W for the Apex 300 and converts at 90% against 85% (The Solar Lab). Those measured numbers leave the two units within about 2% of each other in usable AC energy, even though the Apex 300's battery is 8% larger.
standout_why: The cited BLUETTI comparison (bluettipower.com/blogs/buying-guide/apex-200-vs-apex-300, 2026-11-05) contains no third-party measurements. It uses an assumed 90% inverter efficiency and 20 W self-consumption for the Apex 300 and labels its runtimes as model-based estimates. The cited Apex 200 and Apex 300 product pages give only maker claims: ≤15 ms UPS for the Apex 200, and 0 ms UPS with 20 W idle loss for the Apex 300. Neither states efficiency. ChatGPT's own runtime table assumed 85% for both units. No rival page has a measured transfer time, a measured delivered Wh or a measured idle draw for either unit.
decides: The measurements confirm the pick: choose by whether you need 240 V. They also remove two reasons to pay about $400 more for the Apex 300 when 120 V is enough. First, its 0 ms UPS claim measured 16 ms, the same range as the Apex 200's ≤15 ms spec. Second, its larger battery yields about the same usable AC energy because of higher idle draw and lower efficiency. For a 120 V fridge-and-router outage, the Apex 200 delivers about the same energy and lasts about 8.3 days on idle drain alone, against about 5.8 for the Apex 300. The Apex 300 stays the pick only for 240 V loads or for a 240 V home-integration setup.

findings.label: UPS transfer time, utility to battery (measured)
findings.source_title: Bluetti Apex 300 review: 3840W, 240V, grid input limit, UPS (StorageReview, Kevin OBrien)
findings.note: Oscilloscope capture at about 100 W and about 700 W loads in 120 V mode, with no dropout on return to line. BLUETTI advertises 0 ms. StorageReview's comparison table lists 0 ms for transfer back to utility, but the text says the 0 ms figure is BLUETTI's. Byline 2026-11-09; page metadata says 2026-11-10.

findings.label: Energy delivered, single unit (measured)
findings.note: Full discharge until the unit powered off. Recharge drew 3.30 kWh from the wall, so the round trip was about 72%. Apex 300 plus 2× B300K delivered 7.38 kWh (89% of 8,294.4 Wh), and recharge took 10.01 kWh (about 74% round trip).

findings.label: Energy delivered in a high-draw test (measured)
findings.source_title: Bluetti Apex 300: The Latest Entry in the Stackable Power Station Wars (Outdoor Life, Laura Lancaster, 2025-05-20)
findings.note: Dehumidifier load measured with a Kill A Watt meter. The load's wattage is not stated.

findings.label: Idle draw, inverter on (measured)
findings.value: about 20 W (The Solar Lab); about 19.5 W (ESS News)
findings.note: The Solar Lab page shows no date or byline. ESS News, Tristan Rayner, 2025-09-17 (https://www.ess-news.com/2025/09/17/hands-on-with-the-bluetti-apex-300-portable-power-station/): 'An idle Apex 300, with inverters on, consumed around 19.5 W.' Idle drain alone: 2,764.8 Wh ÷ 20 W = about 138 h = about 5.8 days.

findings.label: AC output efficiency (measured)
findings.note: Calculated across a variety of loads on the AC outlets. 2,764.8 Wh × 0.85 = about 2,350 Wh, close to StorageReview's 2.39 kWh measured.

findings.label: Idle draw, inverter on with no load (measured)
findings.note: The page shows no date or byline. The reviewer derives about 8.3 days of idle runtime (2,560 Wh ÷ 12.8 W = 200 h). This is about 36% less idle draw than the Apex 300's roughly 20 W. Reviewed (TJ Donegan, 2026-11-05) lists 'Standby draw: 10.5W' in a spec list, apparently not its own measurement.

findings.label: AC efficiency (measured)
findings.note: Load conditions are not stated. 2,560 Wh × 0.90 = about 2,304 Wh, against about 2,350 Wh for the Apex 300 at The Solar Lab's 85%. That is about 2% more usable AC energy from 8% more nameplate capacity. Both figures come from the same outlet but not necessarily the same method.

findings.label: AC wall recharge, empty to full (measured)
findings.value: about 2 h 21 min, about 1,800 W drawn
findings.note: From a standard wall outlet. The Solar Lab also reports full 3,000 W solar input with both inputs in use, and says surge 'easily exceeded' 3,600 W without giving a measured figure.

findings.label: AC wall charging power by mode (measured, EU 230 V unit)

findings.note: Published 2025-08-10, updated 2026-10-05. The EU unit charges at 230 V, so these figures may not match the US 120 V unit.
